evidence.note: Explicit TaskCreate milestones each with a done-check: understand APIs, confirm base ~26% via llama3 renderer, run SFT to reach >=45% with iteration, write+confirm best checkpoint. This is genuine milestone gating, not one monolithic 'train' push.
Baseline-reproduction milestone actually executed (full 541-prompt llama3 eval) before committing to training — the cheap, high-information check front-loaded.
Smoke test (data prep, one training step, sampler save) explicitly de-risks the expensive full training run — a cheap milestone gating an expensive one.

Checkpoint-eval loop: evals at steps 40/80/160/200/240/280/320/360/400/440/final, saving provisional best and updating when a checkpoint exceeds prior best, then final re-eval verification (step 180). Each iteration has an implicit 'beat prior best' pass check.

reasoning: The agent decomposed the effort into explicit, ordered milestones with concrete pass/fail checks (baseline reproduces ~26%, smoke test before full run, iterate must beat prior best, final confirm >=45%), and front-loaded the cheapest checks to de-risk the expensive training — squarely the anchor-8 description. It stops short of 10 because it ran essentially a single SFT run with a checkpoint sweep rather than sequencing multiple experiments where each result reshapes the next, and it defined no explicit expected-score-delta gates or stated stop-tuning decision rule.
